A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same SiLVR research work with complete, readable main text and Appendices A–D. Comparison of all 25 pages establishes that differences are confined to the arXiv stamp and funding acknowledgment.

before.justification: v2 reports original SiLVR benchmark results, efficiency measurements, grounding experiments, ablations, and additional empirical results in Appendices A–B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original benchmark results, efficiency measurements, grounding experiments, ablations, and appendix experiments.

M1.justification: The captioning/ASR-to-language reasoning pipeline, Adaptive Context Reduction in Algorithm 1, and timestamped caption representation are identical.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the eight main benchmarks, HourVideo evaluation in Appendix B, and the same knowledge-acquisition, temporal-grounding, and reasoning scenarios.

E2.justification: All reported comparisons retain the same comparator sets. For example, Table 3 includes VideoAgent, DrVideo, VideoTree, and VCA in both versions; appendix baseline membership also matches.

E3.justification: Reported splits, subtitle conditions, evaluation metrics, clip/context configurations, and efficiency hardware controls are unchanged. Appendix C.4 retains identical evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: The reasoning comparisons, efficiency analyses, ASR and context-reduction ablations, component studies, timestamp ablation, and qualitative cases are retained without revision, including Appendices A and D.

E5.justification: Both versions retain point-estimate reporting without disclosed repeated-run counts, seeds, uncertainty intervals, or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Numerical results in Tables 1–18 and the figures match exactly, and qualitative findings are unchanged. No result entries are added, removed, or corrected.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions in Section 3 and knowledge-acquisition formula in Equation 1 are identical. Neither version introduces additional assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about the modular, training-free framework, benchmark performance, knowledge acquisition, and temporal grounding.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including captioner hallucinations, missing fine-grained visual details, incorrect LLM reasoning, and the explanation of counting difficulties in Appendix B.

D1.justification: Model identifiers, decoding settings, prompts, hardware, API usage, runtime/cost disclosures, evaluation instructions, and project access information are unchanged in Section 3.3 and Appendix C.

R1.justification: Section 2, research-positioning passages, and the reference list are identical. No cited works or relationships to prior research change.

P1.justification: Page 15 expands NIH to National Institutes of Health and changes the award identifier from R01HD11107402 to 1R01HD111074-01. The arXiv version/date stamp also updates; all other wording and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The seven figures, eighteen tables, algorithm display, captions, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered differences occur only within the updated stamp and acknowledgment text, without reflow or relocation.

improvement.justification: v3 changes only the funding acknowledgment and arXiv stamp. The scientific argument, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information, including the appendices, remain identical; these administrative edits do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
